correctness.policy: Every SQL record uses the selected API. Query collection is external for every record. No failure allowlist, mixed API routing or un-authored skips are accepted.

binding.statistic: YJIT source ABBA uses mean of two process medians; final interpreter/ZJIT and actual binding comparisons are fresh single-process observations. All measured queries consume their entire result.
binding.callback_note: Buffered native callbacks use 64-row batches, whereas the Rust wrapper buffers all 500 rows in this fixture. Both return identical values and costs and consume every row; their batch-call counts are intentionally recorded separately.

canonical_file.statistic: Source ABBA uses mean of two process p50 values from unchanged canonical per-operation measurements. Characterization/cross-core are single process per lane. Cold-open means a fresh database handle, not cold OS caches.
canonical_file.validation_scope: Canonical rendered-value checksums and consumed row counts; this adapter does not prove exact cost or column metadata equality.
canonical_file.cross_core_retry: Ruby, Go and TypeScript retain the original cross-file measurements. Rust alone was measured in cross-file-rust-retry.json after a separately bounded offline prebuild; all measured queries retain the 512 MiB cap.

blocking.statistic: YJIT means of two process medians in original-source/final/final/original-source order; microseconds per complete query. Other runtimes are single-process final-source characterizations, not before/after estimates.
caveats: Four APIs and both work_mem budgets fully drain the same disk-backed queries; max_query_memory_bytes is unlimited to isolate work_mem.
All timing precedes scratch-I/O and hash-row tracing. Actual scratch writes and reads are positive under 64 KiB and absent under 8 MiB.
Fixtures and scratch files are private, disk-backed and removed after use. Read-only fixture digests match across all workers.
This is a modest blocking-query checkpoint, not cold-OS-cache or whole-engine memory-limit evidence.

cross_memory.statistic: Single fresh process per core, median of five samples, microseconds per complete query.
cross_memory.validation_scope: Rendered-value checksums and row counts only. These adapters use their existing collectors, including Ruby Rows#rows; exact costs and column metadata are independently checked against the Rust Ruby package in the binding reports.

permission_retry.reason: The default sandbox denied local page-service Unix socket creation; this unchanged file-only worker was rerun with explicit escalation.
permission_retry.note: All four initial workers failed opening their database before query timing. The successful memory and host binding measurements were retained; only the unchanged file worker was retried.

rust_file_preparation_retry.reason: The original Rust adapter build exceeded the query-sized 512 MiB cap. Prebuild the unchanged adapter offline with 1 GiB RSS, then retain the original 512 MiB cap for all measured queries.
